lesson.title: Charts and summaries that tell the truth
lesson.subtitle: Bars or lines, mean or median, and charts that mislead

video.title: Charts and summaries that tell the truth
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: The head's chart; Doubled!; Axis from 50. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The head teacher showed us a chart: maths marks had doubled this year! Then I read the axis. It started at fifty.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Charts and summaries that tell the truth
scenes.narration: Today: charts and summaries that tell the truth.

scenes.visual: A bar chart that draws itself: 12, 15, 9, 11 (Monday's rain at four schools (mm)).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Pick the chart for the question
scenes.narration: Pick the chart for your question. Bars compare groups, like Monday's rain at four schools. A line shows change over time, like attendance week by week. And a table is fine when people need the exact numbers.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Count: how many; Mean: add up, share out; Median: the middle, sorted.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then summarise. The count says how many. The mean, or average, adds everything up and shares it out equally. The median is the middle value once you sort them.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “As marked” (Mean 13; Median 13) and “15 typed as 150” (Mean 40!; Median 13). Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Five marks out of twenty: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen. The mean is thirteen, and so is the median. Now one mark is typed as one hundred and fifty instead of fifteen. The mean jumps to forty, out of twenty! The median stays at thirteen.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Median: hardly moves; Mean: dragged along; Look at the chart first; A far dot? Ask why.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The median resists a wild value; the mean gets dragged along. That's why you look at the data, or its chart, before you trust any summary. A dot far from the others is a question to ask, not a number to average.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Bars that don't start at zero; Missing weeks; A summary with no chart.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Charts can mislead without a single wrong number. A bar axis that starts at fifty makes a small rise look huge. Missing weeks hide a bad patch. And a summary with no chart hides the glitches.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Five marks, and one was typed as one hundred and fifty instead of fifteen. Which summary barely moves?

scenes.visual: One big value: 13, The median, typo or not.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The median. It's the middle value, so one wild number at the end barely moves it. The mean adds every value, so the typo drags it along. Fix the typo, or report the median and say why.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A soil sensor in the garden; Loose wire: 0, then 100; The chart shows it at once. Mr Okafor beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Glitches jump out on a chart
scenes.narration: Sensors make the same mistakes. In our school garden, a loose wire made the soil sensor read exactly zero, then exactly one hundred. On the chart, those dots jump out at once.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Spot the red dots; Leave them out; Lowest: 0 → 55.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, a week of soil readings. Spot the red dots, then leave them out. Watch the lowest reading jump from zero to about fifty-five, while the median doesn't move.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. I want to show our school's attendance week by week, across the whole term. Which chart should I draw?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Bars compare, lines show change; Mean or median: know which; Bars start at zero; Chart before summary. Takeaway bar: Every summary hides something; the chart shows what.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A line chart: it shows change over time. Remember: bars compare groups, and lines show change. The median stands firm when the mean is dragged. And look at the chart before you trust a summary.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A bar chart on the board; Axis from zero; Mean and median together; Which tells our story?. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: turn your class survey into a bar chart on the board, with the axis starting at zero. Work out the mean and the median with your pupils. Then ask: which one tells our story better, and why?

checkpoints.prompt: Five marks out of 20; one was typed as 150 instead of 15. Which summary barely moves?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the median is the middle value, so one wild number barely moves it. The mean jumps from 13 to 40.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the mean and the total add up every value, typo included. The median, the middle value, stays at 13.

checkpoints.prompt: To show a school's attendance week by week across a term, which chart fits?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a line shows change over time, week by week.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the question is about change over time, and that's what a line chart shows.
